title: Freedom and Its Price · Why read this book?

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Who carries the costs created by freedom?

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: This essay investigates freedom through choice, responsibility, and unequal power.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: It asks who can act and who bears the consequences of other people’s decisions.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Philosophical arguments meet scientific questions and ordinary social situations.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The discussion considers the relationship between personal autonomy and collective obligations.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Institutions and unequal opportunities complicate apparently simple accounts of individual choice.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The central tension concerns the conditions and costs of living freely together.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: This invitation is for readers interested in political freedom and its social consequences.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Read Freedom and Its Price to follow the complete argument, examples, and consequences.
